notes:
Summary: Enterprise procurement focused on dedicated GPU pools for low-latency fraud decisions and large-scale embedding ops. Key ask: firm throughput guarantees + clear SLA credit schedule. They want reserved capacity in us-east-1, VPC-only access, and the ability to burst to public pool during peak end-of-month processing windows.

Recent timeline (bulleted):
- 2026-01-30: Initial discovery (AE Samantha O.). high level needs: 8-12 A100-equivalent reserved GPUs, 95th pct latency targets, SOC2 requirement.
- 2026-02-18: Product demo + Fireflies call (ff_2026-02-18_01_sg_demo). Showed dedicated capacity UI, autoscale policies, rollback. Client: "we cannot accept opaque fallback without hard guarantees."
- 2026-02-25: Security questionnaire submitted; asked for encryption at rest, KMS/HSM proof, and audit log retention policy (1yr).
- 2026-03-05: Infra deep-dive with SE Diego R. (ff_2026-03-05_infra_review). Discussed VPC peering, NAT egress, cross-AZ failover. Identified potential bottleneck in egress rules for batch embedding jobs.
- 2026-03-10: Pricing & SLA workshop. Legal sent initial redline request on uptime, credits, maintenance windows.

Use-case & requirements (concise):
- Workloads: real-time fraud scoring (chat-style low-latency inference paths for human review), nightly embedding pipeline for transaction clustering, reranking candidate models for decisioning.
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile end-to-end token latency <= 120ms for inference pipeline used in fraud scoring; tail-safety for bursts (99th <= 350ms).
- Throughput: baseline sustained 500 qps across model fleet during peak hours; ability to burst to 2k qps for 2-4 hour windows.
- Reserved GPU planning: initial commit requested for 10 A100-equivalent GPUs with autoscale headroom of +30% burst via dedicated pool or managed bursting to hosted pool. Preference for predictable commit-based pricing (monthly reserved).
- Routing/fallback: must support pinned model versions and explicit canary rollouts; fallbacks acceptable only to pre-approved model variants in same jurisdiction.

SLA negotiation points discussed:
- Uptime: Customer requests 99.99% monthly uptime for dedicated cluster; Redwood proposed 99.95% with credits.
- Credit schedule: Customer wants linear financial credits reaching full pro-rata refund at <99.5%; Redwood proposed tiered credits (0.5% credit between 99.9-99.95, 2% between 99.5-99.9, 10% <99.5). Legal redline expected.
- Maintenance windows: Customer requires maintenance not to reduce capacity during EOD processing windows (23:00-02:00 EST). Wants advance notice >= 14 days for any disruptive maintenance and ability to opt into a maintenance freeze for billing month (paid option).
- Support SLA: P1 response <= 15 minutes (phone/Slack), P2 <= 4 hours, P3 <= 24 hours. Included desire for an assigned escalation engineer during go-live window.

Security & compliance notes:
- Must pass SOC2 Type II attestation; additional ISO27001 is a plus.
- Data residency: transaction payloads must remain in-country for US entities; want log-level residency controls.
- KMS integration required for key management; customer prefers AWS KMS + HSM-backed option.

Open actions / next steps (short):
- Samantha to deliver redlined SLA + SOW by 2026-03-18.
- Diego to produce VPC peering runbook and estimated egress topology impact by 2026-03-16.
- Legal teams to set 1:1 call to reconcile credit schedule week of 2026-03-22.
- POC scope: 2-week dedicated capacity POC (4 A100 equiv) to validate 95th pct latency and burst patterns; customer expects POC report with latency histograms and kernel-level profiling.

Quote from CTO (paraphrase): "We need guarantees we can build on — credits are fine but we need maintenance windows and predictable capacity during month-end runs."

Stumbling blocks: legal liability cap, definition of downtime (is degraded perf downtime?), and exact semantics of 'burst' bridging dedicated vs hosted.

- Provide a clear credit ladder that matches customer's expectations (add a mid-tier at 99.7).
- Add a paid maintenance-free month option and dedicated escalation engineer during go-live.
- Include detailed VPC peering checklist and runbook as part of SOW.
